title: GPU tenant degradation simulator and IaC contracts cheat sheet
author: Mateo Ruiz
body:
Overview:

This cheat sheet documents the GPU tenant degradation simulator (GTDS) — a lightweight, reproducible test harness used by infra engineers to model and validate how tenant-facing inference services degrade under constrained capacity, networking stress, and Terraform/IaC policy changes. The goal is to provide a single-page reference with runnable steps, CI gating patterns, IaC contract checks, telemetry assertions, and operational playbook snippets.

Scope:
- Simulate tenant-level capacity pressure (warm-pool exhaustion, preemption, burst-to-spot fallback).
- Model network degradations (egress shaping, NAT exhaustion, packet loss).
- Validate Terraform/IaC changes that affect GPU pools, NAT gateways, and burst orchestrator policies.
- Verify CI/CD gating rules and telemetry-based alerts that should prevent dangerous rollouts.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Reproducible scenario container images + Terraform workspace per test.
- Coverage: cold-start latency increases, kv-cache miss-rate, token throughput loss, and tail-latency regressions.
- CI policy: any IaC change that increases 95th-latency by > 20% in the simulator must block merge.
- Telemetry contract: simulator emits the same metric names as production (inference.tokens_generated_total, runtime.kv_cache_hit_ratio, network.egress_errors_total).

Key components (short):
1) GTDS harness (service: infra/gtds) — Go binary + k6 traffic profiles that drive realistic inference patterns (mix of short-chat, long-context, streaming).
2) Injector VM set — small fleet of emulated tenants that hold ephemeral KV state and open long-lived connections to the runtime under test.
3) Network shim — eBPF-based traffic shaper for per-tenant egress shaping and synthetic packet loss.
4) IaC workspaces — per-test Terraform directory that can apply/destroy a sealed, isolated GPU-capacity topology (uses tfcloud-ephemeral-account pattern).
5) CI adapter — Jenkins/GHA job templates that run the harness and compare results to golden thresholds.

Run instructions (quick start):
1) Prepare environment:
   - git clone git@github.com:redwood-infra/gtds.git
   - export GTDS_ENV=staging-sim-<your initials>-$(date +%s)
   - ensure you have Terraform service account with ephemeral creds: run scripts/get-ephemeral-creds.sh
2) Start a baseline topology (30m warm pool, 4 regional NATs):
   - cd infra/tf/workspaces/gtds-baseline
   - terraform init && terraform apply -var="warm_pool_size=30" -var="nat_count=4" -auto-approve
3) Launch the harness (30m test):
   - make build && ./bin/gtds run --topology ./topologies/baseline.yaml --duration 30m --metrics-prefix gtds.baseline
   - tail logs: kubectl -n gtds logs -f deploy/gtds-runner
4) Apply stress variant (warm-pool drain + egress noise):
   - terraform apply -var="warm_pool_size=8" -var="egress_shaper_profile=loss-5pct" -auto-approve
   - ./bin/gtds run --topology ./topologies/drain-then-burst.yaml --duration 30m --metrics-prefix gtds.drain
5) Gather results and compare (local CLI):
   - ./bin/gtds compare --baseline gtds.baseline --variant gtds.drain --asserts asserts/ci-block.yaml

Assertions and thresholds (suggested):
| metric | block threshold | warn threshold | note |
| inference.95_latency_ms | > +20% | > +10% | 95p tail latency is primary SLO for interactive tenants |
| runtime.kv_cache_hit_ratio | < -15% absolute | < -7% | decline indicates bad prefix caching or incorrect cache seeding |
| network.egress_errors_total | > 100 / minute | > 20 / minute | NAT or proxy exhaustion flag |
| inference.tokens_per_second | < -25% | < -10% | protects throughput-sensitive batch pipelines |

Example asserts/ci-block.yaml (YAML shown inline):
```
# asserts/ci-block.yaml
asserts:
  - metric: inference.95_latency_ms
    comparator: relative_increase
    threshold_pct: 20
  - metric: runtime.kv_cache_hit_ratio
    comparator: absolute_decrease
    threshold_pct: 15
```

CI/CD integration (recommended pattern):
1) PR workflow (GHA):
   - Step A: Run unit IaC checks (tf fmt, terraform validate, tflint).
   - Step B: Spin ephemeral TF workspace (ephemeral creds), run terraform plan; capture plan delta against current baseline.
   - Step C: Kick GTDS in ephemeral overlay mode (10–30m); run short smoke + tail-latency probe.
   - Step D: Run comparators using asserts/ci-block.yaml. If any assert fails, post failure and block merging.
2) Promotion gates: successful PR must be promoted to a longer nightly run (2–4h) for changes touching burst or scaling modules.
3) Canary rollout (post-merge): patch releases require a staged rollout with automatic rollback if production telemetry mirrors simulator regressions.

Terraform / IaC contracts and checks (patterns):
- Contract A: warm_pool_size must have a minimum value set in module defaults (no implicit null). Example: var "warm_pool_size" { default = 10 }
- Contract B: nat_gateway_count must be >= 2 for any public egress topology.
- Contract C: any change to module gpu_pool.* must include a tfplan annotation explaining risk and expected impact on inference.
- Contract D: module outputs must expose telemetry hooks: metrics_exporter_endpoint and otel_resource_name.

Example Terraform snippet (module wrapper):
```
module "gpu_pool" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-infra/terraform-modules.git//gpu-pool?ref=main"
  warm_pool_size = var.warm_pool_size
  tenant_tag = var.tenant_tag
  metrics_exporter_endpoint = format("https://metrics.%s.internal", var.region)
}
```

Network considerations (operational):
- Per-tenant NAT allocation: prefer per-tenant SNAT pools for high-throughput tenants. Default: 64 ephemeral ports per tenant NAT.
- Egress shaping: use the network shim to simulate 99th percentile ingress-to-egress RTT increases of up to +200ms to model multi-region failover.
- BGP / Transit: tests should include a transit-flip scenario where a region’s egress path is rerouted for 5 minutes to detect session churn.

Telemetry and dashboards (what to compare):
- Primary: inference.95_latency_ms, inference.error_rate, inference.tokens_per_second
- Secondary: runtime.kv_cache_hit_ratio, cache.evictions_total, network.egress_errors_total
- Supporting: infra.tf_apply_duration_seconds, ci.gtds_run_time_seconds, tfplan.change_count

Runbook snippets (when simulator shows regression):
1) Triage (5m): compare variant metrics to baseline; tag failing asserts and owners.
2) Short-term mitigation (15m): if latency spike correlates with warm_pool decline, increase warm_pool_size + scale replica count by 20% via emergency tf apply (use emergency service account).
3) Network mitigation (30m): if NAT exhaustion seen, route affected tenants to a fallback NAT pool (tf variable nat_pool_fallback = true) and enable egress proxy scaling.
4) Rollback (TBD): revert IaC change and re-run GTDS to validate restoration.

Owner and escalation matrix:
- Primary owner: gpu-fleet-team@redwood.internal (oncall: gpu-fleet-rotation)
- Network lead: netops@redwood.internal
- IaC policy owner: infra-iac-team@redwood.internal
- Escalation: if incident extends > 60 minutes with customer impact, notify SRE Pager and Customer Success.

Best practices and tips:
- Keep topologies small and declarative: prefer small ephemeral accounts over modifying prod-like tenants.
- Use deterministic seeds in traffic workloads to make runs comparable. Add `--seed` flag to gtds run.
- Record full tfplan JSON: attach to PR for reviewers to quickly determine proposed resource delta.
- Maintain a golden artifacts bucket with baseline metrics for each major release (path: s3://redwood-gtds/goldens/<release>).

CI templates (copy-paste):
- .github/workflows/gtds-smoke.yaml: runs on changes to terraform modules/** and modules/gpu-pool/**. Uses action redwood/ephemeral-terraform to create a workspace, then runs `gtds run --duration 15m --topology smoke`. Compare with asserts and post status.

Appendix A — common failure patterns and quick remediations:
- Symptom: sudden kv_cache_hit_ratio drop with steady token generation. Cause: cache seeding disabled in module change. Remediation: revert seeding-related tf var, reapply, and run gtds seed-only mode.
- Symptom: bursted tenants hit 429s and network.egress_errors_total spikes. Cause: NAT port exhaustion. Remediation: allocate per-tenant SNAT, increase NAT gateway count, and deploy egress proxy autoscaling.
- Symptom: 95p latency regresses only under long-context tests. Cause: batching parameter change or kv-cache eviction tuning. Remediation: review runtime config (batch.max_tokens, kv_cache.max_entries) and roll forward a kernel tweak in a canary.

References and related artifacts:
- repo: git@github.com:redwood-infra/gtds.git
- tf modules: git@github.com:redwood-infra/terraform-modules.git//gpu-pool
- dashboard: infra -> GTDS Simulator (grafana link internal)
- contact: #infra-gtds on Slack

Notes: keep this cheat sheet focused on reproducibility and gating; longer design docs belong in eng-infra/runbooks or terraform-and-iac folders. If you extend GTDS harness, add an entry to the runbook index and include a small tutorial for new engineers.
